Wakeup handler body plus dequeue path and lifetime of per CPU wakeup queue entries
Virtualization technology for directed IO posted interrupt bypass attach and unblock request mechanics
Trust domain and virtual CPU initialization triggers plus transitions among observed states

findings.text: A common dispatcher selects confidential versus conventional guest execution and initialization need based on guest type, delegating trust domain cases to dedicated helpers and all others to virtual machine extensions helpers.

Guest entry is provided through flavor specific run wrappers and a put wrapper invoked when a virtual CPU is released, with a non instrumentable region covering the actual transition plus interrupt state handling around it.

Interrupt deliverability queries are available for confidential guests using halt exit plus a guest supplied blocked indicator with an always deny fallback variant, and for virtual machine extensions guests using nested behavior plus flags and shadow state.

Other components may use register intercept control, branch record enablement and passthrough management, entry flag computation, guest debug control sampling, exit interrupt information access, write intercept testing, and non instrumentable NMI handling.
Confidential guest helpers expose initialization need, host extended state restoration, failed entry detection, busy status testing, and fast path exit handling for contention cases.

Preparation for blocking requires interrupts disabled and a clear suppress indicator, results in the virtual CPU being queued on its CPU wakeup list and the descriptor notification field naming the wakeup vector, and compensates a race where a notification arrived on the old vector with a self wakeup signal when an outstanding indicator is present. The notification update uses an atomic compare exchange on a once sampled control word.

Wakeup vector switching applies only where posted interrupts can target a blocked virtual CPU, namely interrupt virtualization usable on non confidential guests or directed IO posted interrupts usable when the kernel owns the interrupt chip plus bypass support exists and at least one possible bypass interrupt is counted.

Conventional blocking is absent for nested guests that exit on interrupts and otherwise follows the flags interrupt enable plus move shadow and sti shadow indicators, while confidential guests are treated as always allowed except a halt exit carrying a blocked indication, with a build variant that always reports not allowed.

Host state restoration is a no op unless guest state is marked loaded, otherwise it accounts a reload, restores kernel GS base and relevant segment selectors plus descriptor table state, and clears loaded markers including user return register tracking for the conventional path. The put path also releases posted interrupt state before host restoration.

A confidential virtual CPU is considered needing initialization unless both its own state and its trust domain state report ready, and entry is declined while a sept zap wait flag is set. Forced immediate exit requests are unexpected for this flavor and only provoke a one time warning.

Confidential entry and exit runs with interrupts off inside guest state markers, captures exit reason plus qualification extended qualification address and interrupt information from the secure call results, performs NMI arrival processing, and on return restores host debug control when filtered bits exist plus host extended state for protection keys and feature masks only on divergence, while clearing unavailable register availability except an architecturally preserved set.

Secure call outcomes outside a small set of success and non recoverable statuses map to an invalid exit encoding, and recognized call leaves for identification halt IO and register access preserve their leaf as the exit reason while a guest initiated call versus host call selector distinguishes virtual call exits; a memory violation leaf maps to a misconfiguration encoding whose fatal handling is deferred out of non instrumentable context. Failed entry requires both a failure flag and a valid encoding.

Conventional entry refuses direct execution while emulation is required by synthesizing an invalid state failed entry with default qualification and cleared interrupt information, keeps host address space identifiers and protection controls coherent with current CPU state immediately before entry, honors single step by clearing interrupt shadow, and coordinates pause loop window updates, dirty register synchronization, debug register loading, tracing, performance switching, timer or reschedule signaling, and local timer waiting.

After conventional exit the implementation marks enlightened fields clean and records the virtual processor index when enlightened, restores host debug control when present and user segments on some builds, accounts nested runs only for past checking launches without failure while clearing pending state, records launch success, and completes performance global control plus NMI blocking recovery and interrupt completion before fast path dispatch. Any launch failure or failed entry returns without further handling.

Branch record facilities are disabled for confidential guests with null descriptors, otherwise enablement follows a nonzero record count and passthrough follows presence plus active state of the backing event with intercept changes for source destination optional info select and stack registers; mismatches such as guest tracing enabled or counter still marked in use without a usable event produce a rate limited warning and leave passthrough disabled.

Register intercept state has no effect without bitmap hardware, otherwise read and write interceptions honor an allow filter and any change forces nested recalculation plus clears an enlightened clean marker when enlightened. Write interception is assumed when bitmaps are unused. Entry flags reflect launch history, speculation control interception, and a microarchitectural buffer clearing feature with host mapping access. Tracing entry is inert in system mode and otherwise preserves host control and swaps address ranges only while guest tracing is on. Exit interrupt information is cached on first use, and NMI recognition requires valid plus type match.

Queue linkage for wakeup uses a per CPU lock selected by the virtual CPU current CPU with a scheduler out nesting class, held only across list insertion while interrupts are disabled. The nesting documents freedom from deadlock because the handler that takes scheduler locks cannot run during the disabled window.

Observed state includes a posted descriptor with control notification outstanding suppress and pending bitmap aspects, a per virtual CPU wakeup linkage plus descriptor and exit reason qualification and interrupt information, a loaded marker with host kernel GS base and host segment selections plus address space controls, and run control fields for emulation need launch history pause window debug and performance state.

Lifecycle states include uninitialized versus ready for confidential virtual CPUs and trust domains, sept wait blocking entry, busy contention leaving the fast path so outside guest requests can drain, emulation required forcing synthetic failure, unlaunched versus launched selecting launch versus resume, and branch passthrough enabled versus disabled toggled only on change.

Hazards include suppress set before blocking indicating lost wakeup, a race sampling possible bypass interrupts against concurrent attach mitigated by an unblock request path elsewhere, deferred fatal handling for misconfiguration out of non instrumentable context, indefinite requester blocking if busy contention reentered the guest, branch passthrough requested without a usable backing event, and stale host address space or interrupt shadow causing entry failure if not refreshed.

Two posted interrupt notification vectors exist, a normal delivery vector used around confidential entry including timer local interrupt sampling, and a distinct wakeup vector programmed while blocked and used for compensating self signals.

Control encodings include halt invalid state exception NMI memory violation and misconfiguration identification IO register read write virtual call and trust domain call exits, interrupt type and validity masks with sti and move shadow bits, kernel GS debug control tracing branch select and stack and speculation control registers, feature enable and supervisor state masks, and control fields for RIP RSP address space identifiers pause window and exit information.
